claims.statement: At current theta_k, obtain m_k latent completions from the conditional law p(z|y;theta_k). For candidate theta form Q_hat_k(theta)=m_k^(-1) sum_j log f(y,z_kj;theta), and maximize over theta to obtain the next fit. The baseline MCEM calculation replaces the preceding sampled objective at each iteration; it does not recursively average objectives from earlier parameter values.

claims.statement: The Monte Carlo average is taken over complete log objectives or their sufficient statistics before maximization. definition_evidence.locator: Section 3 Eq6, pp.97-98 / PDF4-5; Section 6 Eq30, p.107 / PDF14

claims.statement: Simulate latent completions under the current conditional law and update Q_k(theta)=(1-gamma_k)Q_(k-1)(theta)+gamma_k times the current sample mean of complete log objectives. Maximize Q_k to obtain the next parameter. For the stated curved exponential family, store sufficient statistics instead: s_k=s_(k-1)+gamma_k(S(z_k)-s_(k-1)), followed by theta_k=theta_hat(s_k). evidence.locator: Section 3 Eq6, pp.97-98 / PDF4-5; M1-M5, pp.99-100 / PDF6-7; Section 6 Eq30, p.107 / PDF14

claims.statement: The single-draw stationary-set theorem requires a smooth curved-exponential complete model and maximizer map, exact conditional simulation given the past, finite continuous second moments, step sizes in [0,1] with divergent sum and finite sum of squares, and almost-sure containment of the statistic iterates in a compact subset of their domain. Under those hypotheses the distance to the stated stationary sets tends to zero. Step-size conditions alone do not supply stability, point convergence, a global maximum or observed-likelihood ascent at every iteration.

evidence.locator: Section 6 SAEM1-SAEM4 and Theorem 5, pp.107-109 / PDF14-16

claims.statement: Recursive averaging of the expected objective precedes its maximization. Optional averaging of fitted parameter iterates is a separate operation with additional local stability, moment and step-size conditions. Averaging statistics before a nonlinear maximizer need not equal averaging parameter values. Simulation-iteration uncertainty around a fixed-data solution is distinct from sampling uncertainty of the statistical estimator.

evidence.locator: Sections 5.1 and 7, pp.104-106 and 110-113 / PDF11-13 and 17-20; Eq26 and Eq48-55

method: Sections 2-3 / PDF2-5: MCEM samples m(k) latent completions under the conditional distribution at the current parameter, builds their mean complete log objective and maximizes it. SAEM recursively combines the previous objective with the new Monte Carlo mean using gamma_k; it need not retain all latent samples when sufficient statistics suffice. Batch averaging is within a current parameter, while recursive averaging discounts samples from previous parameter values.

PDF4 Eq6: Q_k=(1-gamma_k)Q_(k-1)+gamma_k sample_mean(log f). Gamma=1 discards the past; gamma=0 freezes the objective. The paragraph printing gamma=0 for ordinary stochastic EM is inconsistent with its own recursion. Do not adopt that statement. A single draw with gamma=1 has the stochastic complete-data-maximization structure; the separate historical SEM identity still needs original sources.

PDF6-8 M1-M5: curved exponential family f(z;theta)=exp(-psi(theta)+<S(z),phi(theta)>); sufficient-statistic domain contains the convex hull, open parameter space, integrability, smooth psi/phi and mean statistic, exchange differentiation/integration, and a smooth maximizing map theta_hat(s). PDF14-16 Section6 Eq30 and Theorem5: S_k=S_(k-1)+gamma_k(S(Z_k)-S_(k-1)), theta_k=theta_hat(S_k). Single conditional draw case uses 0<=gamma<=1, divergent sum gamma, finite sum gamma squared; exact conditional simulation given the past, finite continuous second moments and smoothness. Almost-sure compactness of statistic iterates within their domain is additional, not implied by the step sizes. Conclusion is distance to stationary sets, not arbitrary-start global maximum or monotone observed likelihood.

A failed proposed statistic step is reset inside an initial compact set and the containing-set index expands. Do not equate this with projection onto one fixed feasible set.

PDF20-24 Section8: inexact conditional maximizations require a distinct perturbation argument and MAX1/MAX2 smooth unique global complete-objective maximizer and geometric inner contraction assumptions. limitations: Responsibilities require a positive finite normalizer for each observed x. At positive beta, zero latent-joint entries remain zero; the beta-to-zero limit is uniform only over the positive support. beta=0 makes the displayed parameter objective independent of eta and is not included as an ordinary M-step.
This record concerns finite latent-state sums. Raising a continuous latent density to a power below one need not preserve integrability; that extension requires its own conditions.

Exact block updates concern fixed-beta free energy. They do not guarantee monotonic ordinary likelihood for beta different from one, global optimality, posterior calibration or held-out improvement. Changing beta does not optimize one unchanged objective.

The inverse-annealing schedule decreases beta after an ordinary-EM start and uses held-out decisions. It is not the same schedule as conventional deterministic-annealing cooling, and it is not a stochastic sampling transition with an invariant target. Schedule thresholds and multiplicative factors require an implementation choice.

The source’s perplexity and retrieval comparisons concern selected historical corpora and settings. No automatic prevention of overfitting, speedup, universal benefit or author-code reproduction is claimed.

claims.statement: For observations x with multiplicities n_x, finite latent states z, model parameters eta and a positive inverse temperature beta, minimize F_beta(q,eta)=sum_x n_x*sum_z q_xz*[log q_xz-beta*log p_eta(x,z)]. For fixed eta, on positive joint support use q_xz=p_eta(x,z)^beta/sum_j p_eta(x,j)^beta. For fixed q and beta>0, minimizing F_beta over eta is equivalent to maximizing the expected complete log likelihood; in PLSA this gives the usual normalized expected-count M-step with the tempered responsibilities. At beta=1 the E-step is the ordinary posterior. With 0<beta<1 it is flatter on its positive support. Hofmann’s inverse-annealing schedule first runs early-stopped EM at beta=1, then reduces beta multiplicatively, continues iterations while held-out performance improves, and stops decreasing beta when further improvements cease. At fixed beta, exact block updates optimize that temperature’s free energy; changing beta changes the objective.

The published objective includes a parameter prior, an average of real-data label/data log terms and a separate average of synthetic-data label/data log terms. The GAN architecture is one realization of the augmentation framework, not a requirement for every possible realization.

limitations: The complete-data estimator must be defined on posterior-supported completed data and have the required moments. Empty mixture components, boundary or infinite MLEs, constrained parameter spaces and nonidentifiability need explicit conventions; a conditional mean can leave a nonconvex parameter space.

Conditional expectation is the least-squares approximation to an integrable squared-error target under a fixed law. That fact does not prove decreasing true parameter error, observed-likelihood monotonicity or global convergence across ICE iterations with changing laws.

The Delmas equivalence uses the mean/expectation parameter psi, although the source calls it canonical; its natural parameter phi is distinct. The claim is not automatic for arbitrary coordinates, curved/constrained exponential families or boundary estimates. A nonlinear transformation does not generally commute with conditional expectation.

For Gaussian mixtures, expectation of a complete-data class mean or variance containing a random class count differs in general from a ratio of expected sufficient statistics. The usual Gaussian-parameter ICE update therefore cannot simply be replaced by an EM update without checking the conditions.

Monte Carlo approximation requires valid posterior sampling and appropriate convergence conditions. Correlated Gibbs samples, finite sample counts and apparently steady parameters do not by themselves certify exact expectations or convergence. A one-sample version can resemble stochastic EM for a specific complete-data estimator; it is not every stochastic-approximation EM algorithm.

The inspected examples in Delmas contain scaling/covariance notation issues, and its introductory suggestion that mixed discrete-continuous data make likelihood irrelevant is not adopted. The definition and qualified coordinate comparison do not certify all printed example formulas. Source complexity statements linear in K are not adopted for arbitrary dense kernels. Positive evidence and careful support handling are required; numerical scaling reduces but does not eliminate all numerical risks.

The source’s Equation(10) omits the complement needed for a minimized Hamming loss, and Figure4 prints argmin where Equation(11) correctly uses argmax of a posterior. Its preliminary prior pass requires root-to-leaf order. This record uses consistent sum-product/max-product semantics rather than those literal displays.

Equations(26)–(27) print an extra state-count divisor, conflicting with the earlier theta>1/K restriction. Active parameter constraints, zero expected counts and emission degeneracy need separate treatment.

The exact posterior factorization in Equation(29) supports ancestral sampling after subtree messages. The experimental H-MCEM uses a local-observation conditioning shortcut and constructed coarse observations; those samples are not certified exact draws from the original posterior. SMAP is a different loss with an approximate procedure, not an alias for exact joint MAP or MPM.

Quadtree image priors can create location-dependent block artifacts. EM remains initialization-sensitive and need not find a global optimum. The selected synthetic, flood and microscopy examples establish application context, not universal segmentation superiority, a modern benchmark or a reproduced implementation.

For finite hidden states, an upward likelihood message is L_s(x_s)=b_s(y_s|x_s)*product_child_t sum_(x_t) A_t(x_t|x_s)*L_t(x_t). The root posterior is proportional to pi*L_r, and each child posterior conditional is proportional to A_t*L_t for fixed parent. Propagating the root posterior downward gives node and edge marginals. Replacing child sums with maxima and retaining maximizing states yields joint MAP by backtracking; independently maximizing node marginals gives MPM and can select a different configuration.
